points.statement: Degradation-aware processing should span the entire pipeline from patch sampling through token transformation to pixel reconstruction.
points.quote: Focusing on these drawbacks, we argue in this paper that degradation-aware processing should span the entire pipeline, from patch sampling, through token transformation, to pixel reconstruction.

points.statement: The principle is to make patch boundaries and reconstruction functions depend on local degradation severity.
points.quote: This suggests a simple but under-explored principle: make patch boundaries and reconstruction functions of local degradation severity.

points.statement: A lightweight degradation encoder predicts a global degradation vector and a spatial degradation map from local degradation severity, which jointly condition patch embedding and unembedding through adaptive deformation.
points.quote: Specifically, FIT employs a lightweight Degradation Encoder to predict a global degradation vector 𝐠\mathbf{g} and a spatial degradation map 𝐌\mathbf{M} from local degradation severity, which jointly condition the patch embedding and unembedding through adaptive deformation.

points.statement: A task-token dropout strategy regularizes task conditioning during training to improve robustness across degradation types.
points.quote: Moreover, to improve robustness across degradation types, we introduce a task-token dropout strategy that regularizes task conditioning during training.

points.statement: A degradation encoder extracts a global vector and a spatial map from a degraded image.
points.quote: Given a degraded image, the Degradation Encoder extracts a global vector 𝐠\mathbf{g} and spatial map 𝐌\mathbf{M}.
